definitions.explanation: A seat that has been booked or set aside in advance at a restaurant, theater, train, or other venue.

examples.japanese: テーブルに「{予約席|よやくせき}」の{札|ふだ}が{置|お}いてあった。
examples.english: There was a 'Reserved' sign on the table.

examples.japanese: {予約席|よやくせき}は{窓側|まどがわ}にご{用意|ようい}しております。
examples.english: Your reserved seat has been prepared by the window.

examples.japanese: {人気|にんき}のレストランなので、{予約席|よやくせき}を{取|と}っておかないと{週末|しゅうまつ}は{入|はい}れない。
examples.english: It's a popular restaurant, so you can't get in on weekends without reserving a seat in advance.

notes:
A compound of {予約|よやく} (reservation) and {席|せき} (seat). You will often see this word written on table placards at restaurants.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {予約席|よやくせき}を{取|と}る (to reserve a seat)
- {予約席|よやくせき}の{札|ふだ} (reserved seat sign/placard)
- {予約席|よやくせき}にご{案内|あんない}する (to show someone to their reserved seat)

Distinguish from {指定席|していせき} (assigned/designated seat, as on trains), which refers to a specific numbered seat purchased with a ticket, and {自由席|じゆうせき} (non-reserved/free seating).
